ambiguous.why: Modern double-extortion ransomware also destroys/alters data and exfiltrates it, so Integrity or Confidentiality is defensible; ISC2 CC doctrine treats denial of access to the asset as the primary loss, hence Availability.
Immutability is often taught as an integrity control; here the stated purpose is surviving ransomware with records reachable, so its primary contribution is availability (recoverability).

ambiguous.item: Keeping a tamper-evident audit log of who changed each record
ambiguous.why: Audit logging is frequently taught as accountability or integrity; within these three buckets the tamper-evident attribution of actions to actors is the non-repudiation construct.

ambiguous.item: Separation of duties on payment approvals
ambiguous.why: Separation of duties is defined administratively but is frequently enforced technically in the payment system; ISC2 CC classifies it as an administrative (managerial) control.

ambiguous.item: A badge-operated turnstile in the lobby
ambiguous.why: Badge systems have a technical/logical access-control component, but the turnstile itself is a physical barrier control, not administrative.

ambiguous.item: A client pressures you to overstate their security posture in an audit report, and you refuse
ambiguous.alternative: Canon III — provide diligent and competent service to principals
ambiguous.why: The client is a principal, so honest service to principals is defensible; the decisive element is truthfulness in reporting, which is Canon II.

ambiguous.item: You tell a client up front that a specialised cloud engagement is beyond what you are qualified to deliver
ambiguous.alternative: Canon II — act honourably, honestly, justly, responsibly and legally
ambiguous.why: Candour about limits reads as honesty; ISC2 guidance places 'do not accept work beyond your competence' under diligent and competent service to principals (Canon III).

ambiguous.item: You report a peer who is selling leaked ISC2 exam questions to candidates
ambiguous.alternative: Canon II — act honourably, honestly, justly, responsibly and legally
ambiguous.why: Reporting dishonest conduct is also honourable/legal behaviour; the harm is to certification integrity and professional reputation, which is Canon IV.
